```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source(here::here("R", "A10", "A10_001-libraries.R"))
source(here::here("R", "A10", "A10_005-share_log.R"))
source(here::here("R", "A10", "A10_010-compare_shared_current.R"))

a10 <- readRDS(here::here("R_objects", "A10_010_comparison.rds"))

co  <- a10$cuts_old   # July file, on TF
cn  <- a10$cuts_new   # new file, on TR
cal <- a10$calibration
cmp <- cal$comparison
r_sel  <- cmp[cmp$set == "Selected cut points (TR)", ]
r_prTF <- cmp[cmp$set == "Previous cut points (TF, July 2026 file)", ]
r_prTR <- cmp[cmp$set == "Previous cut points (TR)", ]
ss  <- a10$shared_steps
chg <- a10$changes
pts <- function(x) formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = 1)

n_trans <- function(from, to) {
  x <- a10$transitions$n[a10$transitions$Change == paste(from, "to", to)]
  if (length(x) == 0) 0L else x
}

inputs_identical <- a10$rows$n_only_shared == 0 && a10$rows$n_only_current == 0 &&
  a10$inputs$tf_missing_mismatch == 0 && a10$inputs$tf_max_abs_diff < 1e-8 &&
  a10$inputs$d102_mismatch == 0 && a10$inputs$jorm_missing_mismatch == 0 &&
  isTRUE(a10$inputs$jorm_max_abs_diff < 1e-8)
rules_hold <- inputs_identical && a10$rebuild$old_mismatch == 0 &&
  a10$rebuild$new_mismatch == 0

pv <- a10$prevalence
pv_get <- function(y, k, what) pv[[what]][pv$year == y & pv$class == k]
ci_txt <- function(p, lo, hi) paste0(fmt_pct(p), "% (", fmt_pct(lo), " to ", fmt_pct(hi), ")")
pp_txt <- function(d, lo, hi) paste0(fmt_pct(d), " (", fmt_pct(lo), " to ", fmt_pct(hi), ")")
first_year <- min(pv$year)
n_other <- chg$n_changed - n_trans("Normal", "MCI") - n_trans("MCI", "Normal") -
  n_trans("MCI", "Dementia") - n_trans("Dementia", "MCI")
```

# Purpose

This report records the core algorithm classification files prepared for Lindsay Kobayashi (LK) for the HRS-HCAP dementia incidence analysis. On 2026-10-21, Rich Jones, Doug Tommet, and LK agreed to replace the July 2026 file. The new file selects its cut points by a rule written before any result was seen. This report shows what the replacement changes and why. Analysis A10 is the place to record data shares (`R/A10/A10_005-share_log.R`).

# Summary

The July file (`r a10$files$shared`) classifies a person-wave with an unrounded T score below `r fmt_cut(co[["severe"]])` as severely impaired and below `r fmt_cut(co[["moderate"]])` as moderately impaired. No record shows how those cut points were chosen. The new file (`r a10$files$new`) rounds the T score to an integer (TR) and uses TR < `r cn[["severe"]]` and TR < `r cn[["moderate"]]`. These cut points come from a pre-specified rule: match the weighted Manly-Jones dementia and MCI shares in HRS-HCAP Wave 1 within set tolerances, then take the pair with the best dementia agreement. Everything else in the algorithm is unchanged.

In HRS-HCAP Wave 1, the new file's weighted shares are `r fmt_pct(r_sel$share_normal)`% Normal, `r fmt_pct(r_sel$share_mci)`% MCI, and `r fmt_pct(r_sel$share_dementia)`% Dementia, against Manly-Jones shares of `r fmt_pct(cal$target_shares[["1"]])`%, `r fmt_pct(cal$target_shares[["2"]])`%, and `r fmt_pct(cal$target_shares[["3"]])`%. The July file gave `r fmt_pct(r_prTF$share_normal)`%, `r fmt_pct(r_prTF$share_mci)`%, and `r fmt_pct(r_prTF$share_dementia)`%. Across all person-waves 2016 to 2022, `r fmt_n(chg$n_changed)` (`r fmt_pct(chg$pct_changed)`%) change class.

# What was shared

```{r}
#| label: tbl-share-log
a10_share_log %>%
  mutate(Notes = unname(a10_share_notes[date])) %>%
  select(Date = date, File = file, `Sent by` = sent_by, `Sent to` = sent_to,
         Status = status, `Local copy` = local_copy, Notes) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Classification files prepared for LK (email thread \"HRS Algorithmic Dx\").")
```

LK received 2 files. The first (2026-06-11) left person-waves without a class when self-rated memory (HRS item D102, memory compared with 2 years ago) was missing. RNJ asked for D102 to be imputed, following the single-imputation approach used in Manly et al. (2022), and DT sent the second file (2026-07-10) with D102 imputed. This report assumes the July file is the one used in the incidence analysis. The copy checked here (`Data/`, file date `r a10$files$shared_mtime`) was saved from that email. A file prepared on 2026-10-17 with grid-search cut points was withdrawn before it was sent. The new file replaces the July file once it is sent; update its row in the share log then.

# How a class is assigned

A person-wave with a T score is classified from 2 cut points and self-rated memory. Call the severe cut point $\tau_1$ and the moderate cut point $\tau_2$. A score below $\tau_1$ gives Dementia when memory is reported as worse and MCI otherwise. A score from $\tau_1$ to below $\tau_2$ gives MCI when memory is reported as worse and Normal otherwise. A score at or above $\tau_2$ gives Normal whatever the memory report. A person-wave without a T score (most often a proxy interview) is classified from the informant IQCODE alone.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-procedure
tibble::tribble(
  ~Step, ~`July file`, ~`New file`, ~Source,
  "Rows", "HRS Core respondents interviewed 2016 to 2022, all ages", "Same", "A7_075",
  "Cognitive score", "8 Core cognitive items; factor model fitted to HRS 2016, item parameters fixed for 2016 to 2022", "Same", "A7_050",
  "T score", "Factor score adjusted for age, sex, race and ethnicity, and schooling; mean 50, SD 10 in the HRS-HCAP robust normative sample", "Same", "A7_052, A7_055",
  "Score compared with the cut points", "TF, unrounded", "TR = floor(TF + 0.5), integer", "A7_055, A7_060",
  "Self-rated memory (D102)", "Singly imputed when missing", "Same", "A0_019",
  "D102 codes counted as reported worsening", "Worse, don't know, refused, not ascertained (3, 8, 9, -8)", "Same", "A7_060",
  "Severe cut point, tau1", paste0("TF < ", fmt_cut(co[["severe"]])), paste0("TR < ", cn[["severe"]]), "A7_070",
  "Moderate cut point, tau2", paste0("TF < ", fmt_cut(co[["moderate"]])), paste0("TR < ", cn[["moderate"]]), "A7_070",
  "How the cut points were set", "Not documented (April 2026)", "Pre-specified rule, 2026-10-21", "A7_070",
  "No T score", paste0("IQCODE ", a10$jorm_cuts[["severe"]], " or higher: Dementia; above ", formatC(a10$jorm_cuts[["mild"]], format = "f", digits = 1), ": MCI; otherwise Normal"), "Same", "A7_060",
  "Unclassified", "No T score and no IQCODE, or D102 missing when T is below tau2", "Same", "A7_060",
  "ADL and IADL items", "Not in the rule; predictors in the D102 imputation only", "Same", "A0_019"
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Steps in assigning a class, July file and new file.")
```

# Checks

```{r}
#| label: tbl-checks
tibble::tribble(
  ~Check, ~Result,
  "Person-waves in the July file only", fmt_n(a10$rows$n_only_shared),
  "Person-waves in the new classification only", fmt_n(a10$rows$n_only_current),
  "Largest absolute difference in T score (TF)", fmt_sci(a10$inputs$tf_max_abs_diff),
  "T score missing in one version only", fmt_n(a10$inputs$tf_missing_mismatch),
  "D102 differs", fmt_n(a10$inputs$d102_mismatch),
  "IQCODE missing in one version only", fmt_n(a10$inputs$jorm_missing_mismatch),
  "Largest absolute difference in IQCODE", fmt_sci(a10$inputs$jorm_max_abs_diff),
  paste0("July file rebuilt from its own inputs with TF < ", fmt_cut(co[["severe"]]), " and TF < ", fmt_cut(co[["moderate"]]), ": classes that differ"), fmt_n(a10$rebuild$old_mismatch),
  paste0("New classification rebuilt with TR < ", cn[["severe"]], " and TR < ", cn[["moderate"]], ": classes that differ"), fmt_n(a10$rebuild$new_mismatch),
  "New file (Data/) versus the A7 object: classes that differ",
    if (isTRUE(a10$new_file$exists)) fmt_n(a10$new_file$mismatch) else "File not found"
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Identity and reconstruction checks, all person-waves.")
```

The first checks compare the inputs to classification. Both versions hold the same `r fmt_n(a10$rows$n_current)` person-waves, the T scores differ by no more than `r fmt_sci(a10$inputs$tf_max_abs_diff)` T units (rounding in how the numbers were written to the file), and D102 and the IQCODE match. The rebuild checks apply the written rule (`R/A7_060-algorithm_functions.R`) to each version. `r if (rules_hold) "Every class matches, so the two files differ only in rounding and cut points." else "Not every check passes; the counts in @tbl-checks locate the differences."`

# The cut points

The July cut points (`r fmt_cut(co[["severe"]])` and `r fmt_cut(co[["moderate"]])`) first appear in the A7 code committed on 2026-04-17. No code derives them, and DT did not recall how they were chosen. Two rules tested in October 2026 with criteria written before the results (`R/A7_072-domain_quantile_check.R`, `R/A7_073-normative_domain_quantile_check.R`) did not reproduce them.

The new cut points come from a rule fixed on 2026-10-21, before any result was seen (header of `R/A7_070-threshold_calibration.R`). The T score is rounded to an integer, and every integer pair (severe `r min(cal$spec$severe_range)` to `r max(cal$spec$severe_range)`, moderate `r min(cal$spec$moderate_range)` to `r max(cal$spec$moderate_range)`) is evaluated in HRS-HCAP Wave 1 (n = `r fmt_n(cal$n_sample)`, weighted by `r cal$weight`) with the memory and IQCODE rules fixed. A pair is eligible if its dementia share is within `r pts(cal$spec$tol_dementia)` percentage points of the Manly-Jones share and its MCI share within `r pts(cal$spec$tol_mci)` points. Among eligible pairs, the rule takes the highest dementia kappa, then the highest 3-class kappa. `r if (cal$selection_stage == "as specified") paste0(fmt_n(nrow(cal$eligible)), " pairs met the tolerances as specified.") else paste0("No pair met the tolerances as specified, so the pre-specified widening was used (", cal$selection_stage, "; dementia ", pts(cal$tol_dementia_used), " points, MCI ", pts(cal$tol_mci_used), " points); ", fmt_n(nrow(cal$eligible)), " pairs were then eligible.")`

```{r}
#| label: tbl-calibration
tibble::tibble(
  Classification = c("Manly-Jones algorithm (reference)",
                     paste0("July file: TF < ", fmt_cut(co[["severe"]]), ", TF < ", fmt_cut(co[["moderate"]])),
                     paste0("Rounding only: TR < ", fmt_cut(co[["severe"]]), ", TR < ", fmt_cut(co[["moderate"]])),
                     paste0("New file: TR < ", cn[["severe"]], ", TR < ", cn[["moderate"]])),
  `Normal, %`   = fmt_pct(c(cal$target_shares[["1"]], r_prTF$share_normal, r_prTR$share_normal, r_sel$share_normal)),
  `MCI, %`      = fmt_pct(c(cal$target_shares[["2"]], r_prTF$share_mci, r_prTR$share_mci, r_sel$share_mci)),
  `Dementia, %` = fmt_pct(c(cal$target_shares[["3"]], r_prTF$share_dementia, r_prTR$share_dementia, r_sel$share_dementia)),
  `Kappa, dementia` = c("", fmt_k(r_prTF$kappa_binary), fmt_k(r_prTR$kappa_binary), fmt_k(r_sel$kappa_binary)),
  `Kappa, 3-class`  = c("", fmt_k(r_prTF$kappa_3class), fmt_k(r_prTR$kappa_3class), fmt_k(r_sel$kappa_3class))
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Weighted (", cal$weight, ") class shares in HRS-HCAP Wave 1 and agreement with the Manly-Jones algorithm. The 3-class kappa uses quadratic weights. All kappas are in-sample; for the new file the cut points were selected in the same data."))
```

`r if (is.null(cal$bootstrap)) "" else paste0("In ", cal$bootstrap$n_boot, " design-based bootstrap samples, the rule selected the same pair in ", fmt_pct(cal$bootstrap$pct_same_pair), "% and a pair within 1 T point of both cuts in ", fmt_pct(cal$bootstrap$pct_within_1), "% (A7 report). The bootstrap describes stability only; it did not affect the selection.")`

# What the replacement changes

The change has 2 steps: rounding the T score, then moving the cut points. @tbl-steps counts the person-waves each step changes.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-steps
a10$steps %>%
  mutate(`Person-waves changed` = fmt_n(`Person-waves changed`)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Person-waves that change class at each step, all ages, 2016 to 2022 (unweighted). A person-wave can change at one step and change back at the other.")
```

`r fmt_n(chg$n_changed)` person-waves (`r fmt_pct(chg$pct_changed)`%) change class from the July file to the new file: `r fmt_n(n_trans("Normal", "MCI"))` from Normal to MCI, `r fmt_n(n_trans("MCI", "Normal"))` from MCI to Normal, `r fmt_n(n_trans("MCI", "Dementia"))` from MCI to Dementia, and `r fmt_n(n_trans("Dementia", "MCI"))` from Dementia to MCI. `r if (n_other == 0) "No person-wave moves between Normal and Dementia." else paste0(fmt_n(n_other), " person-waves make other changes (see @tbl-crosstab).")`

```{r}
#| label: tbl-crosstab
a10$crosstab %>%
  rename(`July file (rows) by new file (columns)` = Shared) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), fmt_n)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Person-waves by class in the July file and the new file, all ages, 2016 to 2022 (unweighted counts).")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-change-wave
changes_tab <- a10$changes$all %>%
  select(Year, `All, n` = `Person-waves`, `All, changed` = Changed, `All, %` = `% changed`) %>%
  left_join(a10$changes$age65 %>% select(Year, `Age 65+, n` = `Person-waves`,
                                         `Age 65+, changed` = Changed, `Age 65+, %` = `% changed`), by = "Year") %>%
  left_join(a10$changes$hcap %>% select(Year, `HRS-HCAP Wave 1, n` = `Person-waves`,
                                        `HRS-HCAP Wave 1, changed` = Changed, `HRS-HCAP Wave 1, %` = `% changed`), by = "Year") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric) & !Year, fmt_n))
knitr::kable(changes_tab, caption = "Person-waves that change class, July file to new file, by year and sample (unweighted).")
```

The July rule compares TF with a cut point c; the new rule compares TR with a cut point c', which is the same as comparing TF with c' minus 0.5. A class can change only when TF lies between the two. `r if (a10$n_changed_outside_bands == 0) "Every person-wave that changes has a T score in 1 of these 2 bands." else paste0(fmt_n(a10$n_changed_outside_bands), " person-waves that change have a T score outside the 2 bands, which rounding and the cut points alone cannot produce.")` The memory report decides the direction of change, as @tbl-mechanism shows.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-mechanism
a10$mechanism %>%
  arrange(`T band`, `Self-rated memory`, Change) %>%
  mutate(`Person-waves` = fmt_n(`Person-waves`)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Person-waves with a T score between the July and new cut points, by self-rated memory and change in class (all ages, 2016 to 2022).")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-prevalence
pv %>%
  transmute(Year = year, Class = class,
            `July file, % (95% CI)` = ci_txt(p_old, lo_old, hi_old),
            `New file, % (95% CI)` = ci_txt(p_new, lo_new, hi_new),
            `Difference, points (95% CI)` = pp_txt(d, lo_d, hi_d),
            `July file, weighted N (× 1,000)` = format_weighted_thousands(wn_old),
            `New file, weighted N (× 1,000)` = format_weighted_thousands(wn_new)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Survey-weighted prevalence of each class among HRS Core respondents 65 and older, by wave, in the July file and the new file. Weights are the wave respondent weights; 95% confidence intervals use the HRS strata and sampling error computation units (logit intervals for prevalence, linearized intervals for the difference, which is estimated within the same respondents).",
                               weighted_thousands_note))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-weight-excluded
a10$weight_excluded %>%
  mutate(across(-Year, fmt_n)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Classified person-waves 65 and older, and those excluded from the weighted estimates because the respondent weight is 0 or missing.")
```

Among respondents 65 and older in `r first_year`, weighted dementia prevalence is `r ci_txt(pv_get(first_year, "Dementia", "p_old"), pv_get(first_year, "Dementia", "lo_old"), pv_get(first_year, "Dementia", "hi_old"))` in the July file and `r ci_txt(pv_get(first_year, "Dementia", "p_new"), pv_get(first_year, "Dementia", "lo_new"), pv_get(first_year, "Dementia", "hi_new"))` in the new file. Respondents with a respondent weight of 0 or missing (in the HRS, most often nursing home residents) do not contribute to these estimates, although they carry a class in the file.

# Assignment steps worth noting

These steps are the same in the July file and the new file. They are listed because they decide how a class is assigned. Counts of unclassified person-waves refer to the July file.

Self-rated memory is singly imputed with the R package mice (Analysis A0, `R/A0_019-impute_self_concerns.R`), separately for each wave, with 1 imputation (seed 2) and the package default method for a numeric variable, predictive mean matching. Predictive mean matching copies an observed value from a respondent with similar predicted values, so an imputed D102 can be any observed code, including don't know (8), refused (9), and not ascertained (-8), which the rule counts as reported worsening. The predictors are the demographic terms (xP1 to xP7 and their interactions, with the matching terms in later waves), the Core cognitive items, the 16 IQCODE items, HRS items D554 to D556, and 10 functional items from HRS section G (G014, G021, G023, G030, G040, G041, G044, G047, G050, G059), read in `R/A0_012-recode_iadl.R`. In `r first_year`, `r fmt_n(ss$d102_imputed_2016)` of `r fmt_n(ss$n_2016)` person-waves have an imputed D102; `r fmt_n(ss$d102_imputed_2016_complaint)` of these imputed values count as reported worsening, `r fmt_n(ss$d102_imputed_2016_dk_rf_na)` of them as don't know, refused, or not ascertained. (The raw D102 is kept for 2016 only, so the count of imputed values in later waves is not available.) After imputation, `r fmt_n(ss$d102_missing_after_imputation)` person-waves still have D102 missing.

Responses of don't know, refused, or not ascertained count as reported worsening for `r fmt_n(ss$d102_dk_rf_na)` person-waves with a T score. The file assigns a class to `r fmt_n(ss$n_under65_classified)` person-waves younger than 65, although the norms apply from age 65 (`r fmt_n(ss$n_age_missing)` person-waves have no age). `r fmt_n(ss$n_unclassified)` person-waves are unclassified: `r fmt_n(ss$n_unclassified_no_tf_no_jorm)` have neither a T score nor an IQCODE, and `r fmt_n(ss$n_unclassified_tf_no_d102)` have a T score below the moderate cut point with D102 missing.

# Files and code

The report is rebuilt with `Rscript Analysis10_Driver.R` after Analyses A0 and A7. It reads `Data/`r a10$files$shared`` (the file as delivered, kept outside git), `Data/`r a10$files$new`` (written by A7_075, optional), `R_objects/A7_075_algorithm_summary.rds`, `R_objects/A7_075_hrs16_22_long.rds`, `R_objects/A7_070_threshold_calibration.rds`, `R_objects/A7_075_hrs16_hcap.rds`, and `R_objects/A7_005_hrs16_22_merged.rds`, and it writes `R_objects/A10_010_comparison.rds`. The share log is `R/A10/A10_005-share_log.R`; for a new share, add a row there.
